subQuestions.questionText:
Various options are provided as possible answers. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A–D) next to the question number.

A function of the National Benchmark Test (NBT) could be to ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — assess whether potential students qualify for regular entry or extended programmes in a specific course. (1)

The NBT assesses academic readiness so institutions can place applicants in mainstream (regular) or extended/foundation programmes.

options.A: determine a potential candidate's abilities, strengths and weaknesses to follow a specific field of study.
options.B: advise students on what type of financial aid they can access, based on the test results.
options.C: assess whether potential students qualify for regular entry or extended programmes in a specific course.
options.D: enable tertiary institutions to place students in any other field of study that may be available at the time.

subQuestions.questionText: Embezzlement is an illegal act of ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D — secretly taking money that belongs to the company you work for. (1)

Embezzlement is the theft or misappropriation of funds placed in one's trust, typically by an employee. Fraud is obtaining money by deception; extortion is by force or threats; bribery is a reward to influence someone.

options.A: obtaining money, goods or property by deceiving other people.
options.B: getting something, especially money, by force or threats.
options.C: giving or receiving a free reward to influence someone's actions.
options.D: secretly taking money that belongs to the company you work for.

subQuestions.questionText: Examples of health-related components of fitness:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — Muscular endurance, cardiovascular fitness and flexibility. (1)

The health-related components of fitness are cardiovascular fitness, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition. Reaction time and coordination are skill-related components.

options.A: Body composition, muscular endurance and reaction time
options.B: Muscular endurance, cardiovascular fitness and flexibility
options.C: Coordination, cardiovascular fitness and muscular strength
options.D: Cardiovascular fitness, flexibility and body composition

subQuestions.questionText: An evaluation of an impact study is done to ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D — determine the changes as a result of a particular intervention. (1)

Evaluating an impact study measures the actual changes/effects the intervention produced; securing resources, planning steps and assigning roles are done before or during the intervention.

options.A: secure all the resources needed to complete the intervention.
options.B: identify the steps needed to conduct that specific intervention.
options.C: decide who will be in charge of carrying out the intervention.
options.D: determine the changes as a result of a particular intervention.

subQuestions.questionText: The Employment Equity Act (EEA), 1998 (Act 55 of 1998) intends to regulate ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A — psychological testing and assessment of potential employees. (1)

The EEA regulates psychological testing and assessment of employees (permitted only if scientifically valid, reliable and unbiased). Lock-outs and workplace forums fall under the Labour Relations Act; child labour under the Basic Conditions of Employment Act.

options.A: psychological testing and assessment of potential employees.
options.B: the right of workers not to be locked out from the workplace while striking.
options.C: employee participation in decision-making through workplace forums.
options.D: employment of young children under the minimum school-leaving age.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

A condition that can be avoided by drinking water regularly during physical education activities.
subQuestions.memoText: Dehydration. (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

The term describing a person who shows exceptional ability, knowledge and common sense about using modern technology.
subQuestions.memoText: Cyber savvy / tech savvy. (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.

The ability to maintain a controlled body position during a dance movement.
subQuestions.memoText: Balance. (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Answer in full sentences.

Give TWO examples of possible gender inequality practices in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each of TWO responses. Any TWO of:
• Unequal pay for equal work being done.
• Objectifying women and young girls.
• Certain genders mostly doing the unpaid labour.
• Labelling or stereotyping based on gender.
• Unequal gender representation.
• Discrimination based on gender/disability/race/class/age.
• Barriers to leadership positions based on gender.
• Treating women/men/other genders as one homogenous group.
• Considering women as the weaker sex who are unable to cope with work pressure.
• Expectations placed on a specific gender that may negatively impact on them.
• Choosing a specific gender for a job based on confidence instead of competence.
• Owing to affirmative action, men may be overlooked for certain positions.
(2 x 1) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why smoking of cigarettes may have a negative effect on your physical appearance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for ONE well-explained response. Smoking may:
• Result in a lack of oxygen in the blood vessels, which could cause discoloration of the skin / uneven skin tone / bad breath / yellow eyes / stains on nails and fingers / discoloration of gums and teeth.
• Lead to a high concentration of chemicals in the body, which may cause sagging or loss of skin elasticity and deeper wrinkles on the face.
• Disrupt the natural process of hair growth, resulting in hair thinning, loss or baldness in some people.
• Cause a drop in appetite, resulting in unnatural weight loss.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do you think municipalities should amend by-laws regularly?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. Any TWO of:
• The living environment of a community changes from time to time.
• Out-dated by-laws may compromise the health and safety of a community.
• So they remain relevant to the ever-changing needs of the community.
• So the procedures used to regulate the protection of all community members stay effective.
• So the constitutional right to a safe environment is upheld at all times.
(2 x 1) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the importance of setting achievable health and fitness goals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It is important because it may:
• Make it easier to keep yourself on pace, encouraging you to stay accountable to yourself.
• Help you be specific about your goals, giving you a clear idea of the actions needed to reach them.
• Increase your chances of successfully completing your goals, motivating you to set bigger goals as you progress.
• Prevent you from being discouraged by unrealistic goals, helping you stay motivated throughout.
• Ensure that you enjoy what you have to do to reach your goals, preventing frustration and the temptation to give up.
• Make it easier to monitor your progress, helping you remain focused on your goals.
(1 x 2) (2)
subQuestions.topic: Personal lifestyle plan and fitness goals

subQuestions.passageText:
ENTREPRENEURSHIP: PLAN A, B or C?

[The source is a graphic on entrepreneurship and planning — it carries no additional body text beyond its heading.]

[Adapted from www.entrepreneur-headlines.co.za. Accessed on 16 February 2021.]
subQuestions.questionText:
Read the source above and answer the question. Write your answers in full sentences.

Explain why entrepreneurs should be risk-takers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may:
• Push them to reach their business goals, helping ensure the success of their businesses.
• Open up new opportunities that may rescue the business from possible closure or lead to business growth.
• Help them accept failure as part of taking risks, allowing them to see failure as an opportunity to learn and improve.
• Spark innovative ideas to deliver new products or services, ensuring they meet changing customer demands and attract new customers.
• Help them overcome the fear of failure, boosting their confidence to face new challenges.
• Help them discover their strengths and weaknesses, motivating them to learn new skills and build on existing ones.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE way in which a potential entrepreneur could determine if a business opportunity will be financially viable. Motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. A potential entrepreneur could:
• Check whether there is a demand or need for the product/service, to determine if it is marketable and if there is a sustainable client base.
• Identify an appropriate location for the business, to ensure potential clients have easy access.
• Research the competition, to prevent running losses due to an oversaturated market.
• Identify a niche market or small target group, in order to provide a specialised product/service as required by those consumers.
• Determine what the running costs would be (electricity, phone, rent, transport), to ensure a balance between income and expenses.
• Test the business idea beforehand, to determine whether it would be profitable.
• Research how to market the product/service, to ensure the business would succeed.
(1 x 2) (2)

questions.title: SECTION B (Compulsory) — Question 2: The importance of communication
questions.passageText:
THE IMPORTANCE OF COMMUNICATION

Our personalities influence the effectiveness of our communication with others. Therefore, developing appropriate personality traits is necessary to deal with different types of personalities, emotions and conflict situations in life effectively.

Being emotionally healthy does not necessarily mean that you are happy all the time or that you are satisfied with yourself and the relationships you have with others. Rather, it may mean that you are aware of your feelings and thoughts about yourself and those of others.

This awareness and acknowledgement may help you to develop better coping strategies which could be used to deal with conflict or changes in relationships.

[Adapted from www.familydoctor.org. Accessed on 25 January 2021.]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a definition for the term personality.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Personality is any ONE of:
• A combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.
• The characteristic patterns of thoughts, feelings and behaviours that make a person unique.
• A set of emotional qualities, behaviour and attitudes that makes one person different from another.
• Behavioural characteristics, both inherent and acquired, that distinguish one person from another.
• The moods, attitudes and opinions of a person, most clearly expressed in interactions with other people.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that may have contributed to a young person developing positive personality traits during childhood.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each of TWO responses. Any TWO of:
• Consistent disciplinary measures by parents/siblings/teachers/caregivers.
• Disciplinary measures that guided a child in how to respond to a situation appropriately.
• Parents who dealt with a situation or crisis unitedly.
• Emotional support from parents/siblings/extended family/peers.
• Parents or caregivers who dealt appropriately with their own problems and challenges.
• Being influenced by people with positive outlooks on life.
• Having grown up in a loving, well-nurtured environment.
• Being guided by cultural or religious belief systems.
(2 x 1) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how a negative attitude towards life could affect your communication with others.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may cause you to:
• Be judgemental of others, always finding fault when communicating with them.
• Be abrupt, curt or blunt, which limits communication and causes miscommunication.
• Constantly complain about everything, making people avoid communicating or starting conversations with you.
• Always dismiss or disregard what others say, so people no longer want to share information, ideas or concerns with you.
• Exaggerate or make things seem worse than they are, creating anxiety or fear in others when communicating with them.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss why avoiding conflict is not healthy for any relationship.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. It may:
• Prevent people from resolving the conflict, which could only worsen the situation.
• Cause you to become withdrawn or introverted, which may lead to irreconcilable differences.
• Intensify the problem, leading to more or other issues in the long run.
• Add to the existing emotional stress of those involved, increasing the rift between the parties.
• Compromise an individual's true feelings, leading to frustration and anger that affects their health negatively.
• Harm intimacy and closeness, because honest communication is compromised or cut off.
• Cause a breakdown in communication and strained feelings, as trust and honesty are lost in the relationship.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Why do you think compromising may not always be considered to be the most ideal method to resolve disagreements?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. Any TWO of:
• Compromising requires both sides to give up something, so it may result in neither party being truly satisfied.
• If someone uses compromise as a hidden agenda or takes advantage of the other's willingness, a pattern can develop where one person always gets their way or manipulates the other.
• A compromise may be perceived as a weakness, causing people to feel powerless or defenceless.
• Some people outwardly 'compromise' while feeling totally different about the situation, which may lead to resentment.
• A compromise may be viewed as always satisfying the other party, breeding feelings of bitterness towards them.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: How would you improve your way of coping with changes in any relationship? In EACH answer, also indicate how improving these coping skills could help you to accept the changes in your relationships.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award THREE marks each for TWO well-explained responses (strategy + how it works + link to accepting the change). You could:
• Assess how much control you have over a situation by determining what you can take responsibility for, so you can accept the things you are unable to change.
• Accept that experiencing change in life is inevitable, helping you deal better with sudden disappointment and cope with the challenges in the relationship.
• Make a conscious decision not to postpone necessary actions, so you are not overwhelmed and can make peace with your new situation.
• Practise better self-care when experiencing loss, helping you deal with feelings of sorrow and lowering the risk of anxiety about your changed circumstances.
• Be more mindful of your thought patterns, assessing how rational your thinking is so you do not feel doomed by assuming the worst outcomes.
• Envision yourself in the future of these changed circumstances, enabling you to be more hopeful and positive about what lies ahead.
• Remind yourself of transitions you successfully navigated before, so you consider which traits might see you through and realise your strengths.
• See change as an opportunity for growth, focusing on what you can learn and helping you determine your priorities going forward.
• Make yourself aware that a change in a relationship could also be positive, helping you be more adaptive and experience the change as a pleasant transition.
(2 x 3) (6) [20]

questions.title: SECTION B (Compulsory) — Question 3: Surviving examinations
questions.passageText:
SURVIVING EXAMINATIONS

Sitting for an examination has proven to be the most difficult aspect of general student assessment. Most students fail an assessment, not because they do not know the content, but because they cannot effectively respond to the questions within the stipulated time.

Knowing your content does not always mean that you are able to effectively answer examination questions since there are factors, such as managing anxiety, which play a role in determining your success in an examination.

Interestingly, examination writing skills, such as time management, are typical life skills because they could be used to deal with daily life demands.

[Adapted from www.study-help/understanding-question. Accessed on 15 February 2021.]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a definition of the term study skills. (No marks are awarded for examples of study methods, strategies or techniques.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Study skills refer to any ONE of:
• The ability to concentrate and perceive information correctly and accurately in order to remember what has been studied.
• An acquired ability to apply the strategies, methods and techniques learned to achieve one's study goals and study effectively.
• The ability to recall and retain information and new knowledge successfully, producing it in a logical way.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText:
Differentiate between the following action words as used in an examination question paper:
• Illustrate
• Identify
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. Any ONE of:
• When illustrating you give an example by clearly showing what you mean, whereas identifying means to find, name or mention something.
• Illustrating means to explain something in ways that clearly demonstrate what needs to be understood, while identifying involves choosing something from a range of factors.
• To illustrate means to explain something by visual representations, e.g. using a graph, figure or diagram, whereas identifying means to pinpoint or briefly describe the main points.
• When illustrating something you could use comparisons, while identifying means to simply recognise and point out something.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE benefit of planning your responses when sitting for an examination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks for a well-explained response. It may enable you to:
• Focus on what is actually required from a question, so you formulate your responses according to the core instruction.
• Make changes to your answers before compiling the final answer, ensuring your responses are clear and relevant.
• Focus only on the main aspects of the question, so you do not waste time on non-essential information.
• Choose the questions you know well, helping you recall the necessary information with ease.
• Be precise in answering a question, ensuring you give the required detail.
• Organise your thoughts to prioritise the information you present, so you present your facts in a logical, coherent way.
(1 x 2) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which you could deal effectively with anxiety during an examination session.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. You could:
• Take a few moments to do breathing exercises, which may calm your nerves and get rid of feelings of worry.
• Assure yourself that you have studied adequately, which may change negative thought patterns and dismiss the fear of failure.
• First focus on the questions you feel confident about, which may help you set aside insecurities about answering other questions.
• Remind yourself of your future aspirations and why you wish to complete the examination successfully, which may inspire the necessary strength of mind.
• Acknowledge your successes in previous examinations, which may eliminate feelings of worthlessness and boost your confidence.
• Embrace the fact that exam stress is normal for everybody, which may counter your nervousness.
• Accept the challenges common with writing an examination, which may help you take better control of your situation.
• Familiarise yourself with your exam environment, which may help you settle down faster and focus on the task.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Assess how time management skills could assist you to perform effectively in your Grade 12 assessments.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award TWO marks each for TWO well-explained responses. It could enable you to:
• Prioritise your deliverables, helping you meet deadlines and targets for assessment tasks more easily.
• Do proper scheduling and planning of tasks and projects, ensuring timeous completion of all work-related activities.
• Monitor that the time spent on each task is valid, ensuring you do not spend too much time on one task at the expense of another.
• Set realistic goals to complete tasks, helping you reach the outcomes for a day or specific period.
• Distribute your workload systematically, helping you stay organised and manage your workload effortlessly.
• Avoid taking on too many tasks within a given timeframe, enabling you to complete assessments more efficiently.
• Set up your work environment to eliminate distractions, ensuring your time is not taken up by less important activities.
(2 x 2) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: How would you adapt your reading skills to respond effectively to examination questions? In EACH answer, also indicate how that could improve your ability to gain maximum marks for a question.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award THREE marks each for TWO well-explained responses (reading skill + how you apply it + link to gaining maximum marks). You could practise the skill to:
• Do reflective reading (skim and scan) to get the overall meaning of the question and related stimuli and relate it to prior knowledge, giving you an indication of the format and length of answers required.
• Develop your reading speed so you read questions and texts more fluently, absorb information faster, concentrate better and capture the different instructions in one question, ensuring you answer each part successfully.
• Read actively so you also consider titles, subheadings, charts, graphs and captions, determine what you understand, identify key aspects and evaluate relevance, helping you formulate meaningful, substantial responses.
• Read strategically so you improve how you decode information, extract efficient information from a source and construct meaningful information, so you respond within the correct context of the question.
• Read with understanding, ensuring you answer to the depth and extent required and provide the most suitable answers to gain full marks.
(2 x 3) (6) [20]

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 4: The devastation of crises and disasters
questions.passageText:
SECTION C: Answer any TWO questions in this section. Responses must be in paragraphs; marks are awarded only for responses written in full sentences. If all three questions are answered, only the first TWO are marked.

THE DEVASTATION OF CRISES AND DISASTERS

The unforeseen devastation caused by global crises and disasters, such as the Covid-19 pandemic and HIV/Aids, has taken a significant toll on people across the world. The rapid spread of such diseases causes global health crises, which impact severely on the livelihood of people.

Glossary: livelihood — income, employment, businesses and jobs.

[Adapted from https://www.medicalnewstoday.com. Accessed on 29 January 2021.]

Write paragraphs on crises and disasters using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: State FOUR benefits for a person who detects a disease early enough.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. Any FOUR of:
• The chances of making a full recovery are better.
• Unnecessary deaths may be prevented and the odds of surviving are greater.
• Treatment could be more effective.
• A person's quality of life may not be affected as severely.
• Restoring or maintaining good health may not be so costly.
• The condition could be managed or controlled instead of worsening.
• Appropriate lifestyle interventions could be done, leading to a longer, healthier life.
• Harm to other organs may be prevented and overall health protected.
• It may prevent a disease from fully developing.
• The chances of a long-term cure are much better than if the disease has progressed.
(4 x 1) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse the negative effect of people's personal views about infectious diseases on the health and safety of people.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). If people:
• Form their own theories about the disease, it may influence others to believe those opinions, leading to the spread of fake news and confusion about whether to comply with safety regulations.
• Misuse what seems like normal social and economic activity and become complacent, they may engage carelessly with others, putting themselves and others at higher risk of contracting the disease.
• Choose to deny the reality of the disease as a way of coping, they may ignore its devastating effects and unintentionally spread it.
• Argue that it is their right not to disclose their health status while knowing they may infect others, they consider only their own interest and deprive others of their right to be safe and healthy.
• Refuse to trust the scientific evidence and believe the disease is a political conspiracy, they may refuse to comply with compulsory precautions and disregard its seriousness.
• Put their faith entirely in religious or traditional practices, believing they will not contract the disease, they may not trust any other prevention or treatment, leading to unnecessary illness and untimely deaths.
(2 x 4) (8)

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the impact of a crisis, such as the global Covid-19 pandemic, on the current trends in the job market.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses. For full marks (evaluation) a candidate must give a statement and qualify it, then give a second statement and qualify it. Any TWO of:
• There has been an extreme downturn in economic activity that severely hit youth employment; however, this has created an opportunity for many young people to become entrepreneurs and develop innovative ideas that became long-term employment options.
• Economic restrictions caused a massive decline in work-based learning opportunities, amplifying the difficulties young jobseekers already faced; however, many virtual platforms have since been created, giving people alternative access to learning opportunities.
• A greater percentage of young people now compete for one job, advantaging the best-skilled young workers; this forces others to acknowledge their shortcomings and creates opportunities for them to gain new skills.
• Many people lost jobs, took salary cuts or had careers disrupted and must now compete with a new cohort entering the labour force; this spurs many to unlock other talents and entrepreneurial skills, opening a new working world.
• There has been a shift in job-skill demands, forcing workers to rapidly learn new technological skills; this results in higher demand for technical and online crash courses so people can meet the demands of remote work.
• Many companies had to change business strategies to survive the recession and stay relevant; this results in innovative ways to market their business, creating new job opportunities.
• Face-to-face recruitment could no longer happen under lockdown, causing delays in appointments; companies adapted to online recruitment, which became an easier, faster way to connect with candidates.
• Many companies had to work from home to keep delivering services and business; however, working from home has left some workers feeling isolated without colleagues nearby for support.
• Many companies retrenched workers, realising they could operate without certain positions; other companies used the situation to monitor and evaluate employees more closely, holding more people accountable for productivity.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 5: Critical analysis of the media (limitations and accessibility of information)
questions.passageText:
CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE MEDIA

Limitations to freedom of expression ensure public safety, while the increasing digital divide between different groups in society impacts negatively on access to information for all.

Glossary: digital divide — inequalities in access to information and communication technology.

[Adapted from https://www.justice.gov.za. Accessed on 29 January 2021.]

Write paragraphs on limitations and accessibility of information using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: State FOUR ways in which the media could ensure access of information to all communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. The media could:
• Ensure that all print media and subscriptions to electronic media are affordable.
• Accommodate the different language needs of all communities (including braille).
• Liaise with the government telecommunication department to help provide infrastructure and broadcasting towers.
• Increase radio and TV broadcasting by helping to establish more stations and channels.
• Encourage communities to have their own local newspapers, magazines and radio stations.
• Advertise important local and international news on billboards, pamphlets, at community events or via mobile stations.
• Use bulk messaging systems to keep all communities informed of important news.
• Introduce new types of newspapers such as tabloids and free news sheets.
• Provide more efficient delivery and distribution systems to reach more readers.
(4 x 1) (4)

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse how limitations to the right to freedom of expression of the media may assist in promoting public safety.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). By:
• Limiting the overemphasis of criminal incidents in reporting, the media can control the careless use of shocking details, helping keep the public calm and preventing citizens from engaging in violent unrest that endangers lives.
• Ensuring news about local, provincial and national governments is truthful and accurate, government is portrayed fairly, encouraging citizens to trust their government and helping avoid public outrage and violent demonstrations.
• Protecting the identity of children who are victims of abuse or convicted of juvenile offences, children's safety is considered, protecting them from further exploitation by offenders and securing their personal welfare.
• Restricting the broadcasting of upsetting interviews or disturbing photographs of people in protective custody, they feel safe and can trust the justice system, safeguarding them from further victimisation and threats.
• Regulating the publishing of unlawful illustrations of community protests, the media can control outbreaks from spreading, ensuring social order and protecting citizens from harm and property from vandalism.
• Controlling media reporting on national security and public order, the media is obligated to be responsible and limited from publishing information that compromises national security, protecting citizens and the country from possible international threats.
(2 x 4) (8)

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss the impact of the increasing digital divide on different groups in society, specifically the poorer communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). Any TWO of:
• Poorer communities are again left behind in changing technological developments, as they may not be provided with the advanced infrastructure needed for unlimited access to modern ICT, hampering socio-economic development further.
• People in deep rural areas may be unable to apply for jobs advertised on digital platforms because they lack the devices to access them, resulting in rising unemployment and widening the gap between rich and poor.
• Disadvantaged communities have limited exposure to virtual and distance-learning opportunities, so they do not get the quality education they deserve, increasing illiteracy and reducing their chances of qualifying for better jobs.
• Inadequate e-communication increases the remoteness of some groups from civil society, making them feel isolated and progressively apathetic about issues that affect them because they are deprived of opportunities to participate.
• Poorer communities deprived of digital information have their powerlessness emphasised, intensifying their inability to express opinions and disempowering them from decision-making processes that affect their lives.
• Not having free access to information limits the possibility of breaking the cycle of poverty, since knowledge is power; limiting information suppresses citizens instead of integrating all communities into broader society.
• Not everyone knows how to use modern ICT tools, so they cannot bridge these communication gaps or optimally use technology, and the economic status of such communities stays the same.
• The digital divide violates the civil rights of people in poorer communities by causing them to lag further behind in ICT, a clear indicator that their interests are not adequately attended to and contributing to existing poverty.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]

questions.title: SECTION C (Answer any TWO of Questions 4, 5 and 6) — Question 6: Finding meaning in work (the value of work and work ethics)
questions.passageText:
FINDING MEANING IN WORK

Finding work meaningful is something that every worker should experience. However, some people may not find meaning in their work, hence they are most likely to act unethically in the workplace.

[Adapted from https://sloanreview.mit.edu/article/what-makes-work-meaningful-or-meaningless. Accessed on 3 December 2020.]

Write paragraphs on the value of work and work ethics using the three points below as a guideline.

subQuestions.questionText: State FOUR ways in which work could give you a sense of purpose in life.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award ONE mark for each response. Any FOUR of:
• Each day of your life may be filled with daily goals to accomplish.
• You have a specific role to play at your workplace.
• You may learn new skills and experience different things every day.
• You may experience a sense of companionship and belonging with your colleagues.
• It may afford you opportunities to grow as a person and explore alternative career paths.
• You are able to contribute to the economy and your community.
• It may instil feelings of self-worth, accomplishment and significance.
• You may be doing what you love and heeding your calling in life.
• You may feel that your life is valuable and rewarding to yourself and others.
• It could give you balance in life.
• It may offer you certainty, financial and emotional stability, and direction in life.
• You could serve as a role model to other members of your community.
(4 x 1) (4)
subQuestions.topic: The value of work and work ethics

subQuestions.questionText: Analyse why it is necessary for all workers to follow the required ethical behaviour in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). If all workers:
• Do their work with diligence, they strive to continually perform at their best, greatly improving overall productivity and helping achieve the common goal of the company.
• Commit to always functioning efficiently, it lessens frustration among co-workers, creating a sense of a joined workforce and enabling everyone to complete work within the required time limits.
• Take pride in their work, they do it with enthusiasm, ensuring outstanding service delivery and strengthening the integrity of every worker.
• Honour the responsibilities assigned to them, each accepts accountability for their own failures and successes, preventing hostility and enhancing good working relationships.
• Aim to be professional at all times, everyone is encouraged to follow this conduct, helping all workers maintain the same standards and upholding the principles of the company.
• Treat each other with respect under all circumstances, it inspires positive change in how they engage, fostering mindfulness and securing an emotionally safe working environment.
• Show integrity in all they do, they refrain from dishonest practices, preventing fraud and corruption and ensuring everyone maintains high morals in the workplace.
(2 x 4) (8)

subQuestions.questionText: Critically discuss the importance of understanding your core values to ensure that you find meaning in your work.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award FOUR marks each for TWO well-explained responses (statement + elaborate + qualify + outcome). Any TWO of:
• Exploring your core values first is an important step toward setting realistic career goals, as you cannot set a goal without knowing what you are looking for; being aware of your values gives clarity about what you want from life and puts you in a better position to pursue meaningful work.
• Identifying your core values is crucial in making important life decisions, as it enables you to prioritise these values, which guides you to a job that offers what you are looking for and helps you reflect on whether you are following the right career.
• Defining your core values is important when pursuing a job opportunity, since it helps you determine whether your values align with the work values and, if not, whether you could adapt, helping you view job opportunities through the correct lens.
• Your core values are the compass that leads you to a suitable career, so it is vital to revisit them regularly so you do not lose sight of what matters, helping you decide what career moves to make and whether to keep or leave a job.
• Clearly outlining your core values helps you reflect on what is important to you in a job, giving you more guidance when weighing the prospects of a job and making it easier to accept or decline it.
• Your core values help you determine the significance of a specific job to you, and following them early in your career makes it easier to decide which opportunities to consider and find the job that offers the satisfaction you are looking for.
(2 x 4) (8) [20]
